results.title: Day 22: Model Retraining and Feedback Loops in MLOps
results.content: # Day 22: Model Retraining and Feedback Loops in MLOps. ## Day 22: Model Retraining and Feedback Loops. As new data is collected, retraining models and implementing effective feedback loops are critical to maintaining their relevance, accuracy, and efficiency. On Day 22 of our deep dive into machine learning, we focus on model retraining and feedback loops, including how workflows can be automated and the role of tools for incremental learning. ### Why Retrain Models? Model retraining is the process of updating a machine learning model to improve its performance by incorporating new data. ### Feedback Loops in Model Retraining. Incremental learning is a paradigm where models learn continuously as new data becomes available, without requiring retraining from scratch. ### Challenges in Model Retraining and Feedback Loops. Model retraining and feedback loops are essential components of robust and adaptive machine learning systems. By automating retraining workflows and leveraging tools for incremental learning, organizations can ensure their models remain relevant in dynamic environments.

results.title: Ethnographic data-sharing as community building | OUPblog
results.content: # Ethnographic data-sharing as community building. *Life in a New Language f*ocuses on migrants' lived experience of language learning and settlement, features large-scale ethnographic research achieved through unique data-sharing and re-use approach, and offers deep exploration of adult language learning in real life. Instead of rejecting data sharing, ethnographers are uniquely positioned to contribute positively to open research by decentering data and recentering context, community, and lived experience. Data sharing following “FAIR Principles” has widely come to be seen as best practice in research. Even in STEM disciplines working with quantitative data, “data sharing is still mostly an ideal, honored more in the breach than in practice.” This is due to the fact that there is a gap between the ideal of data sharing and research workflows characterized by time pressures and the imperative to compete for scarce resources. As a group, they have low awareness of open research, have no space for the additional time commitments needed to create open data, and often face restrictions from supervisors and more senior colleagues. Therefore, even the possibility of data being made available beyond the confines of the research team—regardless of what the privacy settings of the repository might be—will mean that some participants think twice about participation. To preserve the ontological and epistemological integrity of ethnographic research, data sharing must not only maintain the relationships established in the projects being brought together but extend and enhance them. For the *Life in a New Language* project, we combined data from 130 participants across six separate ethnographic studies conducted over a period of 20 years to explore the lived experience of adult language learning and migrant settlement. We managed to bring the person of the researcher along with the data. Reimagining data sharing as creating a research community of practice enabled us to create new knowledge related to our specific research problem, how adult migrants make a new life through the medium of a language they are still learning. Incidentally, we created a working model for how to combine existing small data sets into a larger longitudinal study of a social phenomenon within an open research framework and a collaborative ethics of care.

results.title: Automating Model Retraining and Deployment for Continuous AI Improvement – AvanSaber
results.content: * Automating model retraining and deployment can streamline the process and ensure timely updates. The automation of model retraining and deployment has emerged as a transformative solution for organizations seeking to streamline their AI operations. While automation offers numerous benefits for AI model retraining and deployment, it also raises important considerations regarding data quality and security. **CI/CD pipelines enable teams to automate testing and deployment processes, ensuring that new model versions are rigorously evaluated before being released into production.** This not only enhances the reliability of updates but also accelerates the pace at which organizations can iterate on their models based on user feedback or changing conditions. **For instance, a leading e-commerce platform adopted an automated model retraining system to enhance its recommendation engine’s accuracy based on real-time user behavior data.** By integrating machine learning algorithms into its existing infrastructure, the company was able to continuously update its models without manual intervention—resulting in improved customer engagement metrics and increased sales conversions over time. Model retraining and deployment in the context of AI refers to the process of updating and improving machine learning models with new data, and then deploying these updated models into production for use in making predictions or decisions. Automating model retraining and deployment is important for enterprises because it allows them to continuously improve their AI models without manual intervention, saving time and resources. Automation can be used to manage model updates, retraining, and redeployment by setting up processes and workflows that automatically trigger these actions based on predefined criteria, such as the availability of new data or changes in model performance. ### What are the benefits of automating model retraining and deployment for continuous AI improvement? The benefits of automating model retraining and deployment for continuous AI improvement include improved accuracy and performance of AI models, reduced manual effort and human error, faster time to market for updated models, and the ability to adapt to changing data and business requirements more effectively. Some best practices for implementing automation in model retraining and deployment include establishing clear criteria for triggering model updates, retraining, and deployment, using version control for tracking changes to models and data, monitoring model performance and feedback loops, and ensuring proper testing and validation of updated models before deployment.

results.title: MCP Model Retraining Workflows: Optimize & Automate 2025
results.content: # MCP model retraining workflows. Learn how to set up and optimize MCP model retraining workflows with automation and best practices for 2025. This is where **MCP model retraining workflows** become essential, serving as the cornerstone of resilient and effective AI systems. ## Understanding MCP model retraining workflows. It provides a unified view and governance layer over all stages, including data preprocessing, model training and versioning, deployment, monitoring, and, critically, maintenance through retraining. An automated retraining workflow ensures that the model adapts to new patterns, maintaining its predictive accuracy and relevance. ## Setting up effective MCP model retraining workflows. Creating a robust retraining workflow is a systematic process that transforms model maintenance from a reactive, manual task into a proactive, automated discipline. Building an effective retraining workflow involves a cyclical process that begins after a model is first deployed. As machine learning systems become more integrated into core business operations, adhering to best practices for model retraining is no longer optional—it's essential for maintaining performance, mitigating risk, and maximizing ROI. The pipeline should automate everything up to the final deployment—running tests, generating a comparison report between the new and old models, and evaluating performance on key data segments. One successful implementation saw a major online retailer build a pipeline that automatically retrains its product recommendation model based on real-time user behavior data. Deploying an automated retraining workflow is a significant technical achievement, but its true value is measured by its impact on model performance and business outcomes. A successful, optimized MCP model retraining workflow finds the economic sweet spot, ensuring that models are updated precisely when the business value of the improvement outweighs the cost of the process itself. ## Future trends in MCP model retraining workflows. The explosion of **Generative AI** has also introduced a new set of challenges and a corresponding sub-discipline known as LLMOps. Retraining and fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) involves unique workflows, such as managing prompt templates, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems, and continuous feedback loops like Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF). **MCP model retraining workflows** have emerged as the critical discipline for ensuring that AI systems remain accurate, reliable, and valuable over time.
